question.problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x-y+2z=5 \\  & 2x-y+7z=7 \\  & x-y+3z=5\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & 5 \\ 2 & -1 & 7 & 7 \\ 1 & -1 & 3 & 5\end{aligned}].
$$

Transforming $M$ to reduced row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & 5 \\ 2 & -1 & 7 & 7 \\ 1 & -1 & 3 & 5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & -3 \\ 1 & -1 & 3 & 5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-3{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}-2{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 0 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x=2 \\  & y=-3 \\  & z=0.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the solution $x=2$, $y=-3$, and $z=0.$ Or, in vector form, $⟨2,-3,0⟩.$
